newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends off fresh 8-1/2 yr high, seen stronger.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends off fresh 8-1/2 yr high, seen stronger.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar posted fresh 8-1/2 year highs on Thursday, peaking at US$0.7161 before drifting lower at the close.
The Kiwi ended at 0.7138/45 and 67.15 on its Trade-Weighted Index, sharply up from 0.7095/02 and 66.94 at the open.

"Obviously a very big day," one dealer remarked. "Quite a large parcel going through there pushed it through some stops, and we also had the combined effects of the Aussie dollar going up quite strongly today and the Kiwi moving in tandem."
The New Zealand currency was now seen supported at 0.7125 with sellers above 0.7150.
Dealers said the settlement of a recent eurobond issue had given the Kiwi a boost but its impressive bounce off 0.7100 this morning suggested it would test higher in the near term.
"It is still looking pretty perky and we're probably looking for a move towards 0.7170 now," the dealer said.
A chief dealer said the Kiwi could test 72 U.S. cents, despite expectations of a easing in monetary policy some time in the next six months.
"Even if New Zealand rates come down by half to one percent, they're still much higher than the rest of the world," he said.
The Kiwi was seen vulnerable to political comments as parties continued to negotiate to form a new government after last month's inconclusive elections, but any selloff was likely to be temporary.
"We certainly will have a reasonable selloff, but once everything comes back to equilibrium it will start going higher again," the chief dealer said.
The Kiwi was seen trading a 0.7125-65 range overnight.
